meta.title: Waves — split expenses with anyone, in any currency
meta.description: Waves splits a bill any way you need, keeps the balance in every currency you spent, and hands the settlement to the payment app you already use. Works with the network off. Free, with no limit on groups or expenses.
meta.ogAlt: Waves — every bill split, every debt settled

banner.text: The whole ledger is free. No card, no trial clock.

hero.subtitle: Waves splits a bill any way you need, keeps the balance in every currency you spent, and hands the settlement to the payment app you already use. It works with the network off.

custody.claim: Waves never holds, moves, or touches your money.
custody.body: It works out who pays whom, hands the amount to the payment app you already use, and records what both sides agreed. That is why it works with any payment method in any country — and why there is nothing here for anyone to run off with.

features.title: Built around the part that goes wrong
features.subtitle: Splitting is the easy half. Waves is designed for the other half — remembering, reconciling, and actually getting paid back.

items.title: Every kind of split, none of the arithmetic
items.body: Equal, exact amounts, shares, percentages, or one person covering someone else. Waves keeps the remainder honest — the split always adds back to the bill, to the last minor unit, because amounts are stored as whole cents rather than as decimals.
points: Equal, exact, shares and percentage splits
Split one bill between two groups of people
Comment on any expense when the memory gets fuzzy
A full edit history, so nothing changes quietly

items.title: Add an expense with no network at all
items.body: Waves writes to your phone first and syncs later. A restaurant with no signal, a flight, a mountain road — none of it stops the ledger. The copy on your device is encrypted at rest, and signing out destroys the key.
points: Everything works with the network off
Conflict-safe sync when you come back
Encrypted at rest on your device
Sign out and the local copy becomes unreadable

items.title: One trip, four currencies, no spreadsheet
items.body: Set the rate you actually got, once, and every expense on the trip converts the same way — so the total at the end matches the total you really paid. Give the trip a budget, a photo album, and a map of where the money went.
points: Fix a rate per bill, per person, or per trip
Trip and per-category budgets that warn before they break
Attach a place to any expense
A shared album for the trip's receipts and photos

items.title: Scan it, or just say it
items.body: Point the camera at a receipt and Waves pulls the line items out on the device itself. Or hold the microphone and say it — "twelve fifty for coffee, split with Nadia" — and the expense arrives filled in, ready to check before it is saved.
points: Receipt scanning that itemises the bill
Voice capture, several expenses in one breath
Capture now with no group, file it later
Keep the photo on your own device if you prefer

items.title: The part where you get paid back
items.body: Waves reduces the web of who-owes-whom to the fewest payments that clear it, then hands the amount to your own payment app. Pay part of it. Attach the proof. Either side can reject a settlement that never happened.
points: The fewest payments that settle the group
Partial and per-expense settlements
Attach proof; either side can cancel or reject
Reminders that do the asking for you

items.title: A private ledger nobody else can see
items.body: Not everything is a group expense. Waves keeps a personal side — your own spending, income, recurring bills, loans and budgets — that never appears in anyone else's copy of the app.
points: Solo expenses and income, kept private
Recurring bills and subscriptions
Loans you gave and loans you took
Monthly budgets with a category breakdown

how.title: Three steps, then it gets out of the way

steps.title: Start a group, share the link
steps.body: A trip, a flat, a dinner, or one person. Send the link or show the QR code — people can join and see the group in a browser, without an account and without installing anything.

steps.title: Add what you spend
steps.body: Type it, scan the receipt, or say it out loud. Waves splits it the way you asked and updates everyone's balance the moment it syncs — or the moment you are back on a network.

steps.title: Settle, and stay friends
steps.body: Waves reduces the web of who-owes-whom to the fewest payments that clear it, opens your own payment app with the amount filled in, and marks it settled once both sides agree.

items.title: Living together
items.body: Rent, power, the internet bill, and whoever always buys the milk. Recurring expenses that reset every month.

items.title: Couples
items.body: A shared ledger for what is shared and a private one for what isn't. Both live in the same app.

items.title: One-offs
items.body: Somebody covered your ticket. Add them as a person — no group, no ceremony — and square it up later.

privacy.title: What Waves can and cannot see
privacy.body: Most apps in this category tell you they take privacy seriously. Here is the same claim written as three lists, including the one nobody publishes.

cant.title: Your money
cant.body: Waves never holds, moves or touches funds. Settling hands off to your own payment app, so there is no balance here to see.

cant.title: The ledger on your device
cant.body: The local copy is encrypted at rest with a key held in your phone's own keystore. It never leaves the device, and signing out destroys it.

cant.title: Your receipts, if you say so
cant.body: Photos can stay on the device, or go to your own Drive, Dropbox or OneDrive. Not to us.

does.title: The shared ledger
does.body: Groups, expenses, splits and settlements are on our server, because that is what lets four phones agree. Everyone in a group can already see all of it.

does.title: An account
does.body: An email address or the identifier your sign-in provider gives us, plus which devices you use, so a stolen session can be revoked.

does.title: Nothing sold, ever
does.body: No advertising, no data sales, no tracking for anyone else's benefit. The free tier is paid for by the paid tier.

wont.title: The people you split with
wont.body: Everyone in a group can see that group's expenses, amounts and comments. Privacy here means privacy from us and from outsiders, not from the group.

wont.title: Losing the device before it syncs
wont.body: An expense that has not synced exists only in the encrypted copy on that phone. If the phone is gone before it reaches the server, so is the expense.

wont.title: Anything on the server side, from us
wont.body: The shared ledger is not end-to-end encrypted. We could technically read it, we have no reason to, and we would rather say so than imply otherwise.

privacy.footnote: Waves has not been through an independent security audit, and this page will say so until it has. Deleting your account deletes the rows, not a flag on a row we keep.

items.a: Yes. Groups, people, expenses, currencies, offline use and settling up are unlimited on the free tier and will stay that way. Plus exists for the features with a running cost behind them — receipt scanning, photo storage and extra devices. There is no card at sign-up and no trial that expires.

items.q: Does everyone need to install the app?
items.a: No. Share a link or a QR code and people can join and see the group in a browser, with no account and no download. They can create an account later if they want the app, and the ledger follows them.

items.q: What happens when I have no signal?
items.a: Nothing stops. Waves writes every expense to your phone first, so adding, editing and splitting all work with the network off. When you reconnect it syncs in the background and reconciles anything that changed while you were away.

items.q: Can Waves handle more than one currency?
items.a: Yes, from the first expense. Every amount is stored in the currency it was spent in, as whole minor units rather than as a decimal, so nothing drifts. You can fix the exchange rate you actually got for one bill, for one person, or for a whole trip.

No, and that is deliberate. Waves works out who pays whom and how much, then hands that to a payment app you already use — a bank transfer, UPI, Pix, SEPA, PayNow, Venmo, PayPal or cash. Your money never passes through us, and Waves is not a bank.

items.q: What do you do with my data?
items.a: As little as we can. The ledger on your device is encrypted at rest, receipt photos can stay on your device or in your own cloud storage, and there is no advertising and no data selling. The shared ledger is on our server because that is what lets several phones agree — it is not end-to-end encrypted, and we would rather say so plainly.

items.q: Which countries does it work in?
items.a: All of them. Waves is not tied to a payment network or a banking licence, so there is nothing to roll out country by country. It speaks English, Tamil, Hindi and Arabic, and handles every ISO 4217 currency.
